candidates.full_text: As awareness of migraine disability is becoming higher, the recognition of the pivotal role of caregivers of people with migraine and their burden is still scarce. We aimed to investigate the factors associated with the distress of informal caregivers of patients affected by high-frequency or chronic migraine with depressive symptoms. All consecutive adult patients with high-frequency or chronic migraine and depressive symptoms were considered, along with their caregivers. Sociodemographic characteristics and the average weekly hours spent together were assessed among patients and their caregivers (dyads). In patients, we evaluated monthly migraine days (MMDs), monthly acute medications (MAMs), pain intensity, migraine-related disability, the composite 4D score on migraine burden, and depressive symptoms (Patient Health Questionnaire-9-PHQ-9). Caregivers filled in the Relative Stress Scale (RSS). The mutuality scale (MS) was also collected in the dyads. 154 dyads (308 participants) were enrolled (patients aged 42.6 years, SD 12.7; 80.5% female; and their caregivers aged 48.1 years, SD 12.2; 36.4% female). The mean shared reported time was 89.7, SD 29.7 h per week. In patients, PHQ-9 scores were higher in those with higher disability scores (MIDAS; p < 0.001), whereas MMDs were not directly related (p = 0.356). The RSS score in caregivers was 20.6 (SD 10.9). Among caregivers' features, the reciprocity subdomain of the MS was inversely related (p = 0.009) to the perceived distress (RSS). The MS total scores and subdomains (p consistently < 0.05) were highly related within the dyad. A positive, mild relation was observed between caregiver RSS and patient PHQ-9 (r = 0.197; p = 0.014) and 4D (r = 0.234; p = 0.004) scores. Finally, when both caregiver and patient characteristics were included, the caregiver reciprocity MS subdomain (p < 0.001) was the main factor associated with RSS scores. The MI-DEAR study highlighted the elevated perceived distress of caregivers of hard-to-treat patients with migraine and depressive symptoms. Low caregiver reciprocity, more severe patients' depressive symptoms, and multidimensional migraine burden were associated with higher caregivers' distress. The study was preregistered on clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07029126 on Jun 11th 2025. © 2026. The Author(s).

candidates.full_text: Traditional preventive treatments for migraine have limitations (e.g., efficacy, adverse events [AEs], contraindications, and interactions). The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 2 rimegepant dosing regimens relative to placebo as preventive treatment for episodic migraine. This was a phase 4, randomized, placebo-controlled study. Adults with a ≥1-year history of episodic migraine (with or without aura) and 4-14 migraine attacks/month were enrolled from outpatient/research sites in 10 countries. After a 28-day observation phase, participants were randomly assigned to placebo once daily, rimegepant 75 mg every other day/alternating placebo, or rimegepant 75 mg once daily for 12-weeks of double-blind treatment. The primary end point was mean reduction from the observation phase in monthly migraine days over the entire 12-week double-blind phase analyzed using linear mixed effects modeling. Hierarchical testing was used for key secondary end points to control type I error. Safety assessments included AEs. Participants (n = 692; median age 44.0 years, 86.7% female) were treated double blind with rimegepant every other day (n = 232), rimegepant once daily (n = 229), or placebo (n = 231). The primary end point was met for both rimegepant dosing regimens, with significantly greater reductions from the observation phase in monthly migraine days over the entire double-blind phase vs placebo (least squares mean change difference [97.5% CI]) for rimegepant every other day (-0.6 [-1.22 to -0.01], p = 0.0220) and rimegepant once daily (-1.8 [-2.35 to -1.19], p < 0.0001). All 5 key secondary end points were significant vs placebo for rimegepant once daily ( p < 0.0001), while for rimegepant every other day, the first key secondary end point in the hierarchy was not significant vs placebo. Most AEs were mild or moderate. Both rimegepant dosing regimens were superior to placebo for the preventive treatment of migraine and were well tolerated. This study demonstrates the efficacy and safety of rimegepant 75 mg QD in a double-blind study. The study was not designed to directly compare the rimegepant EOD and QD dosing regimens. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05217927 (clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05217927); registered January 20, 2022; first enrollment March 4, 2022. This study provides Class I evidence that in adults with more than 1-year history of episodic migraine and 4-14 migraine attacks/month, both rimegepant 75 mg every other day and rimegepant 75 mg daily were superior to placebo in reducing monthly migraine days up to 12 weeks of follow-up.

candidates.full_text: Eptinezumab is a calcitonin gene-related peptide monoclonal antibody (CGRP mAb) for migraine prevention, offering rapid onset and quarterly intravenous administration. However, evidence regarding patient and healthcare professional (HCP) experiences and its implementation in routine practice remains limited. This study has explored the opportunities and challenges of eptinezumab treatment. This convergent mixed-methods study was conducted at King Chulalongkorn Memorial Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. A total of 20 patients with migraine who received eptinezumab and 10 HCPs participated. Monthly headache days (MHDs) and Migraine Disability Assessment (MIDAS) scores were evaluated over 6 months for patients. Semi-structured in-depth interviews explored experiences with eptinezumab treatment for both participant groups, with transcripts analyzed using thematic analysis. Median MHDs decreased from 18.5 (IQR 8.5-28.0) at baseline to 5.0 (2.0-8.0) at Month 3 and 2.5 (1.0-5.0) at Month 6. Median MIDAS scores decreased from 63.5 (30.0-77.5) to 15.0 (1.0-33.0) and 5.0 (0.5-19.5), respectively. Qualitative findings identified three opportunities: improved migraine symptoms and quality of life, favorable treatment experience and acceptability, and addressing unmet needs in patients with migraine who had experienced multiple preventive treatment failures. Patients and HCPs described improved migraine control, restored daily functioning, and favorable tolerability. Three major challenges emerged: financial and access barriers, health-system and service delivery challenges, and treatment-related concerns. High costs and limited reimbursement were the predominant barriers identified by both participant groups. Patients and HCPs perceived eptinezumab as an effective and well-accepted preventive treatment. Although quarterly intravenous administration was viewed favorably, financial barriers and healthcare system constraints remain major obstacles to broader implementation. These findings offer practical insights into integrating CGRP-targeting therapies into routine care. NCT07035197 (ClinicalTrials.gov). © 2026. The Author(s).

candidates.full_text: Headache disorders are common neurological conditions with numerous treatment options depending on the specific disorder and the needs of the individual. Psychedelic drugs, such as psilocybin, dimethyltryptamine and lysergic acid diethylamide, have important historical roles in headache medicine and are re-emerging as potential therapeutic options, particularly in cluster headache. The renewed interest in psychedelic treatment for headache is largely attributable to the patient community, who have advocated for their preferred forms of treatment, including psychedelic drugs. Clinical trials in cluster headache and migraine have supported the reported efficacy and safety of psilocybin in the transitional treatment of these disorders, and additional studies of other compounds and modes of treatment are ongoing or on the horizon. In this Perspective, we provide an overview of psychedelic drugs in headache medicine, including historical context, relationship to conventional headache medications, and the limited clinical and scientific evidence to date. Safety, logistical and legal concerns are also discussed to set the stage for future work in the field. © 2026. candidates.full_text: Migraine and endometriosis are chronic pain disorders that mainly affect women of reproductive age and co-occur more often than expected by chance. Evidence suggests this comorbidity reflects shared biological mechanisms rather than a direct causal link. This perspective examines overlapping pathways, including estrogen-dependent pain regulation, genetic susceptibility related to hormone signaling and inflammation, neuroimmune interactions, and peripheral and central sensitization. Genetic studies show modest but consistent shared heritability, especially involving genes linked to estrogen receptors, inflammatory pathways, and nociceptive processing. Hormonal fluctuations across the menstrual cycle influence neuronal excitability and immune responses in both conditions. Emerging data indicate that calcitoningene-relatedpeptide-mediated neurogenic inflammation may be a key converging mechanism connecting hormonal regulation, immune activation, and pain amplification, though its role in endometriosis is less established. Understanding these shared pathways may improve diagnosis and support more integrated, mechanism-based treatment strategies. Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Inc.

candidates.full_text: BackgroundThese post-hoc analyses evaluated the proportions of participants who experienced sustained responses to atogepant, an oral calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist, over two 3-month, double-blind, randomized controlled trials (RCTs) (ELEVATE and PROGRESS) and a 12-month interim analysis of the open-label extension (OLE) study that was composed of participants from ELEVATE and PROGRESS.MethodsPost-hoc analyses were conducted to assess the sustained responses with atogepant 60 mg once daily (QD). Sustained responses, based on predefined thresholds for reductions in monthly migraine days (MMDs) over a specified period, allow for evaluation of long-term efficacy of atogepant. The ELEVATE trial enrolled participants with episodic migraine who had inadequate response to two to four classes of conventional oral preventive medications; the PROGRESS trial enrolled participants with chronic migraine. These post-hoc analyses were conducted in the modified intent-to-treat (mITT) populations for the atogepant 60 mg QD group from the RCTs ELEVATE (151 participants) and PROGRESS (256 participants). An initial response was defined as ≥ 50%, ≥ 75%, or 100% reduction in MMDs from baseline to month 1 of each respective RCT. Proportions of participants who maintained or exceeded their month 1 response threshold through months 2 and 3 of each RCT were calculated. For the OLE, (ELEVATE, 240 participants and PROGRESS, 284 participants in the mITT population), initial response was defined as ≥ 50%, ≥ 75%, or 100% reduction in MMDs from baseline to month 4 of the OLE. Proportions of participants who maintained or exceeded their month 4 response threshold at month 12 of the OLE were calculated.ResultsIn the two 12-week RCTs, 61.3% (49/80) of ELEVATE participants and 74.2% (69/93) of PROGRESS participants who experienced an initial ≥ 50% reduction in MMDs during month 1 of each RCT continued to have a ≥ 50% reduction in MMDs during both months 2 and 3. During the OLE, 83.4% (121/145) of participants from ELEVATE and 88.5% (131/148) of participants from PROGRESS who experienced a ≥ 50% reduction in MMDs from the RCT baseline to month 4 of the OLE continued to have a ≥ 50% reduction in MMDs at month 12 of the OLE. High rates of sustained responses were similarly observed across the other response thresholds.ConclusionsParticipants who experienced an initial clinically meaningful response with atogepant continued to experience sustained responses over the 3-month RCTs as well as at 12 months of their OLE study.Trial registrationELEVATE (3101-304-002), NCT04740827 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04740827?cond = ELEVATE,%20NCT04740827&rank=1&tab = results), 2021-02-05; PROGRESS (3101-303-002), NCT03855137 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03855137?cond = PROGRESS,%20NCT03855137&rank=1&tab = results); 2019-02-25; Open-label Extension (3101-312-002), NCT04686136 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04686136?cond = NCT04686136&rank=1); 2021-02-19.

candidates.full_text:
Background
          Evaluation of company clinical trial reports could provide information for meta-analysis at the commercial introduction of a new technology.
        
        
          Methods
          Clinical trial reports of sildenafil for erectile dysfunction from September 1997 were used for meta-analysis of randomised trials (at least four weeks duration) and using fixed or dose optimisation regimens. The main outcome sought was an erection, sufficiently rigid for penetration, followed by successful intercourse, and conducted at home.
        
        
          Results
          Ten randomised controlled trials fulfilled the inclusion criteria (2123 men given sildenafil and 1131 placebo). NNT or NNH were calculated for important efficacy, adverse event and discontinuation outcomes. Dose optimisation led to at least 60% of attempts at sexual intercourse being successful in 49% of men, compared with 11% with placebo; the NNT was 2.7 (95% confidence interval 2.3 to 3.3). For global improvement in erections the NNT was 1.7 (1.6 to 1.9). Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 30% of men on dose optimised sildenafil compared with 11% on placebo; the NNH was 5.4 (4.3 to 7.3). All cause discontinuations were less frequent with sildenafil (10%) than with placebo (20%). Sildenafil dose optimisation gave efficacy equivalent to the highest fixed doses, and adverse events equivalent to the lowest fixed doses.
        
        
          Conclusion
          This review of clinical trial reports available at the time of licensing agreed with later reviews that had many more trials and patients. Making reports submitted for marketing approval available publicly would provide better information when it was most needed, and would improve evidence-based introduction of new technologies.

candidates.full_text: Over the past 12 years there have been 12 randomised control trials, involving 843 infants, evaluating the effect of salbutamol or albuterol on bronchiolitis. Of these, nine (75%) showed that bronchodilators had no effect. In three studies a small transient improvement in the acute clinical score was seen. Ipratropium bromide had no significant effect. There have been five recent randomised trials involving 225 infants, evaluating the effect of nebulised adrenaline (epinephrine) on bronchiolitis. All five (100%) have shown significant clinical improvement, with reductions in oxygen requirement, respiratory rate and wheeze after nebulised adrenaline. Two showed lower hospital admission rates and earlier discharge with adrenaline. A significant improvement in pulmonary resistance was observed after nebulised adrenaline but not after salbutamol or albuterol. Currently there is no compelling evidence that bronchodilators have a role in the routine management of infants with bronchiolitis. There is better evidence for the use of nebulised adrenaline.

The intent of the list is to assist growers in distinguishing those pesticide products whose labels do not legally prohibit use on cannabis from those that clearly do not allow use. The list is not an endorsement or recommendation to use these products in the production of cannabis in Oregon. Do not hesitate to contact Pesticide staff with questions or for label clarification. 

***Alert regarding the use of pyrethrins and/or piperonyl butoxide***

Recent lab results show high levels of the active ingredients pyrethrins and/or piperonyl butoxide in some cannabis samples. Pyrethrins and piperonyl butoxide are on ODA's Guide List for Pesticides and Cannabis. ODA is investigating why some samples indicate levels of one or both of these pesticides, which far exceed the Oregon Health Authority (OHA) Action Levels, and yet others do not. To retain the listing of these two pesticides on the Guidelist, ODA, OHA, and Oregon Liquor Control Commission (OLCC) need to learn more about what influences pesticide residue levels on cannabis. If you used pyrethrins and/or piperonyl butoxide, and your cannabis tested below OHA’s Action level, please contact ODA at (503) 986-4553.

candidates.full_text: Postmenopausal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) with oral oestrogen was predicted to reduce coronary heart disease (CHD) risk by 50%. Randomized controlled trials show no such benefit, however, pointing instead to an initial increase in CHD events. Although the cardiovascular effects of transdermal HRT are largely unknown, improvements in arterial function are maintained when oestrogen is administered transdermally. Transdermal HRT also avoids the increased plasma levels of C-reactive protein (CRP) that are seen with oral HRT. However, the clinical significance of this general reduction in hepatic over-synthesis of plasma proteins is difficult to assess. Nevertheless, the available evidence on transdermal HRT appears to justify a formal clinical trial.

candidates.full_text: Clinical trials are critical in advancing medical treatments but often suffer from immense time and financial burden. Advances in statistical methodologies and artificial intelligence (AI) present opportunities to address these inefficiencies. Here we introduce Prognostic Covariate-Adjusted Mixed Models for Repeated Measures (PROCOVA-MMRM) as an advantageous combination of prognostic covariate adjustment (PROCOVA) and Mixed Models for Repeated Measures (MMRM). PROCOVA-MMRM utilizes time-matched prognostic scores generated from AI models to enhance the precision of treatment effect estimators for longitudinal continuous outcomes, enabling reductions in sample size and enrollment times. We first provide a description of the background and implementation of PROCOVA-MMRM, followed by two case study reanalyses where we compare the performance of PROCOVA-MMRM versus the unadjusted MMRM. These reanalyses demonstrate significant improvements in statistical power and precision in clinical indications with unmet medical need, specifically Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). We also explore the potential for sample size reduction with the prospective implementation of PROCOVA-MMRM, finding that the same or better results could have been achieved with fewer participants in these historical trials if the enhanced precision provided by PROCOVA-MMRM had been prospectively leveraged. We also confirm the robustness of the statistical properties of PROCOVA-MMRM in a variety of realistic simulation scenarios. Altogether, PROCOVA-MMRM represents a rigorous method of incorporating advances in the prediction of time-matched prognostic scores generated by AI into longitudinal analysis, potentially reducing both the cost and time required to bring new treatments to patients while adhering to regulatory standards.

candidates.full_text: Novel dose-finding designs, using estimation to assign the best estimated maximum- tolerated-dose (MTD) at each point in the experiment, most commonly via Bayesian techniques, have recently entered large-scale implementation in Phase I cancer clinical trials. We examine the small-sample behavior of these "Bayesian Phase I" (BP1) designs, and also of non-Bayesian designs sharing the same main "long-memory" traits (hereafter: LMP1s). For all LMP1s examined, the number of cohorts treated at the true MTD (denoted here as n*) was highly variable between numerical runs drawn from the same toxicity-threshold distribution, especially when compared with "up-and-down" (U&D) short-memory designs. Further investigation using the same set of thresholds in permuted order, produced a nearly-identical magnitude of variability in n*. Therefore, this LMP1 behavior is driven by a strong sensitivity to the order in which toxicity thresholds appear in the experiment. We suggest that the sensitivity is related to LMP1's tendency to "settle" early on a specific dose level - a tendency caused by the repeated likelihood-based "winner-takes-all" dose assignment rule, which grants the early cohorts a disproportionately large influence upon experimental trajectories. Presently, U&D designs offer a simpler and more stable alternative, with roughly equivalent MTD estimation performance. A promising direction for combining the two approaches is briefly discussed (note: the '3+3' protocol is not a U&D design).

candidates.full_text: Background: In settings where proof-of-principle trials have succeeded but the effectiveness of different forms of implementation remains uncertain, trials that not only generate information about intervention effects but also provide public health benefit would be useful. Cluster randomized trials (CRT) capture both direct and indirect intervention effects; the latter depends heavily on contact networks within and across clusters. We propose a novel class of connectivity-informed trial designs that leverages information about such networks in order to improve public health impact and preserve ability to detect intervention effects. Methods: We consider CRTs in which the order of enrollment is based on the total number of ties between individuals across clusters (based either on the total number of inter-cluster connections or on connections only to untreated clusters). We include options analogous both to traditional Parallel and Stepped Wedge designs. We also allow for control clusters to be "held-back" from re-randomization for some period. We investigate the performance epidemic control and power to detect vaccine effect performance of these designs by simulating vaccination trials during an SEIR-type epidemic using a network-structured agent-based model. Results: In our simulations, connectivity-informed designs have lower peak infectiousness than comparable traditional designs and reduce cumulative incidence by 20%, but with little impact on time to end of epidemic and reduced power to detect differences in incidence across clusters. However even a brief "holdback" period restores most of the power lost compared to traditional approaches. Conclusion: Incorporating information about cluster connectivity in design of CRTs can increase their public health impact, especially in acute outbreak settings, with modest cost in power to detect an effective intervention.

candidates.full_text: Large language models have made a powerful case for the reach of statistical inference. They produce fluent language, solve heterogeneous problems, and exhibit forms of abstraction that cannot be dismissed as simple retrieval. Their success, however, does not establish that inference is sufficient for intelligence. That conclusion follows only by sliding between distinct ideas: inferential competence, task performance, agency, and phenomenal awareness. This essay separates them. It argues that inference is always organized by a prior structure of relevance-a specification of which distinctions, errors, goals, and outcomes matter. In biological agents, that relevance is continually shaped through self-maintenance, embodied action, developmental history, and exposure to the consequences of action. Present language models largely inherit it from humangenerated corpora, training objectives, prompts, evaluation procedures, and deployment institutions. They therefore possess what I call borrowed worldliness: genuine competence acquired from the traces of human engagement with the world, without yet displaying the autonomous normative organization characteristic of ecological agency. Drawing on active inference, ecological psychology, Umwelt theory, and enactivism, the essay develops a substrate-neutral account of this distinction. The argument neither denies the capacities of language models nor rules out artificial agency. It establishes a narrower conclusion: successful inference, even when remarkably general, is not by itself sufficient evidence of an agent for whom anything is at stake.
